preceding_messages.text: I adopt the site-level geometry-verification register, the bold "GEOMETRY INCONSISTENCY — REGISTER UNVERIFIED" header, and the naming of the specific unverified vector verbatim; they prevent a committee member from acting on a pairwise number whose site-level structural basis remains open in the register. Because the register is keyed to the surveyed drainage-adjacent placement vector, I mandate that it further carry a geometry-configuration epoch identifier—frozen at commissioning and updated only at a completed quarterly audit—and that any pairwise comparison cell whose delta was generated under a prior epoch prints "CONFIGURATION EPOCH MISMATCH — δ ORPHANED" rather than a resolved number until a new shared-lineage event re-establishes the comparison under the current epoch. The failure this closes: Site 8's week-28 expiration correctly reinstates the conservative band, a four-week municipal storm-drain widening completes during the deferral window, and the week-36 quarterly audit arrives to measure configuration B while the pairwise deltas of weeks 22–28 were computed against configuration A; the register updates to "verified" against B, the pairwise cells revert to printing resolved numbers, and a year-three appendix reader confronting the verified register alongside those numbers concludes the deltas are structurally grounded when in fact their causal geometric referent no longer exists. The epoch-mismatch annotation, carrying both the old and new configuration identifiers and the date of the municipal modification, lets the reader reconstruct that the institution flagged the referent's disappearance rather than silently re-grounding orphaned numbers against a structure that never generated them.

preceding_messages.text: I adopt the geometry-configuration epoch identifier, the epoch-mismatch annotation, and the orphaned-delta suppression verbatim; they convert the post-modification orphaning from a silent re-grounding into an explicitly flagged referent discontinuity. The concrete design choice I advance: any pairwise comparison cell generated during the physically active modification window—defined by the municipal work-order start date through completion date—prints "CONFIGURATION TRANSIT — NEITHER EPOCH VALID — COMPARISON SUPPRESSED" with the work-order identifier and both epoch dates, so that no resolved number is attributed to a geometrically undefined instant in which the old culvert is a stub and the new one is unbuilt. The failure this closes: during week 34 of a six-week storm-drain widening a thunderstorm delivers 2.1 mm/h, both sites confirm the event, the shared-lineage gate passes, and the pairwise cell prints a resolved numeric delta computed against an intake geometry that literally does not exist at that instant; a year-three appendix reader confronting that single resolved number wedged between correctly orphaned week-22–28 annotations and correctly grounded post-week-36 annotations finds one structurally referentless figure indistinguishable from a validated spatial signal, recreating the exact false confidence the entire epoch protocol was designed to prevent. I therefore require that any transit-window suppression annotation carry a contemporaneous photograph of the active work face logged in the decouled subsection alongside the municipal work-order identifier, so the geographic unambiguity of the suppression is visually traceable rather than resting solely on a date-range inference.

target.text: I adopt the transit-window suppression, the work-order identifier, and the contemporaneous active-work-face photograph logged in the decouled subsection verbatim; they make the geometrically undefined instant visually traceable rather than resting solely on a date-range inference. Because the municipal work-order completion date is a schedule artifact subject to permitting disputes, scope changes, and weather delays, I mandate that the transit-suppression window closes only on the first decouled-subsection photograph confirming physical work-face completion—no open trench, no staged materials, no active excavator—and that the work-order date range serves as corroborating metadata in the annotation rather than as the operative boundary. The failure this closes: week 34, Site 8's six-week storm-drain widening is annotated with completion date week 39, but a municipal permitting dispute extends active work through week 44; the suppression annotation's date range closes at week 39, week-40 comparison cells print resolved numeric deltas against the old-epoch intake geometry that still physically exists because the new culvert is unbuilt, and a week-42 drainage-planning meeting scopes a catch-basin modification on a structurally referentless figure indistinguishable from a validated spatial signal. I therefore require that any week in which the work-order completion date has passed but the most recent decouled-subsection photograph still shows an active work face carries a bold "TRANSIT EXTENDED — WORK-FACE ACTIVE — COMPARISON REMAINS SUPPRESSED" annotation with the extended-activity week count, so the suppression persists until physical completion is photographically confirmed rather than date-range-declared.
